parsed.use_case: Display controllers and camera pipelines must reorient pixel buffers by 90 degrees to match hardware sensor mount angles or device orientation changes. In memory-constrained graphics processors and embedded displays, this reorientation must occur directly within the existing frame buffer without allocating secondary scratchpad memory.
system_examples: Android SurfaceFlinger — reorients display layer buffers during screen orientation changes to match physical panel scanout directions without allocating extra frame memory.
libjpeg-turbo — reorients discrete cosine transform coefficient blocks during lossless JPEG transformations to update photo orientation without allocating duplicate block buffers.
parsed.explanation: The standard solution achieves in-place rotation by transposing the matrix across its main diagonal and reversing each row, preserving O(n²) time while eliminating the O(n²) auxiliary space needed by the naive copy approach. In production graphics and image processing, this in-place manipulation is essential for embedded DSPs and GPU tile caches with strict memory budgets, although high-throughput desktop libraries sometimes deliberately choose out-of-place rotation to optimize sequential memory bus write patterns.
